chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashshab, who said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr narrated to me from Dawud ibn al-Husayn from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding two men who agreed on two just arbitrators and appointed them as arbitrators between them, and a dispute arose between them, and they accepted the two arbitrators, and the two arbitrators differed regarding which of their opinions the ruling should follow, he said: 'Look to the one who is more learned in jurisprudence, more knowledgeable of our hadith, and more pious, and his ruling is executed and the other is not regarded.'

key_terms.أَفْقَهُهُمَا: the one more learned in jurisprudence

ai.seo_question: How is a dispute between two arbitrators resolved in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the criteria for selecting the binding arbitrator among two disagreeing parties are defined not merely by seniority but by a triad of qualifications: deep jurisprudence (fiqh), mastery of our (Shia) hadith, and piety (wara'). This establishes a hierarchical model of judicial authority in Shia fiqh, emphasizing that legal validity rests on the superior scholar's interpretation when consensus among arbitrators fails. The emphasis on 'hadithina' specifically links the legal ruling to the distinct prophetic tradition preserved by the Ahl al-Bayt.
